name: Pololu D24V50F5 5 V, 5 A step-down regulator
description: 5 V, 5 A synchronous buck module for 6–38 V in with an enable pin, sized for servos, motor drivers or a Raspberry Pi on 3S–8S batteries.

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Minimum input rises to about 6.2 V at 5 A.
Switching frequency drops at light load, which can make filtering harder.

terminals.name: EN
terminals.note: Enabled by default: 100 kΩ on-board pull-up to reverse-protected VIN. Drive below 0.6 V to enter low-power state (~10-20 µA per volt on VIN). Leave unconnected if unused.

terminals.name: VIN
terminals.note: Up to 38 V; effective minimum is VOUT + dropout (6 V headline minimum).

notes: The five pins are on one 0.1 in row in the order EN, VIN, GND, GND, OUT, labeled on the top side. A 5x1 straight or right-angle header is included. This module has no power-good pin.
The text says dropout rises roughly linearly from about 0.7 V to about 1.5 V with load. Pololu's dropout graph shows about 1.15 V at 5 A.
Has reverse-voltage protection (no voltage limit stated), over-current and short-circuit protection, thermal shutdown, soft-start and under-voltage lockout.

The over-current limit depends on temperature. At low VIN with sustained loads well over 5 A (more than 5 s), the regulator might not shut off before it is damaged. Pololu suggests a fuse or circuit breaker in that case.
No-load quiescent current is 700 µA typical; with EN low it is 10-20 µA per volt on VIN.
Switches at about 600 kHz. Frequency drops at light load, which can make output noise harder to filter.
Can get hot enough to burn you during normal operation.
Two 2.18 mm mounting holes for #2 or M2 screws.

summary: 6–38 V in → 5 V fixed, 5 A, 600 kHz
